title: Prescriptions & Renewals: days' supply, refills and validity by class
content:
**Medication Management Office standard.** For the Prescriptions & Renewals line, each prescription class sets how large one fill may be, how many refills one new prescription or renewal authorizes, how long the prescription stays valid, the largest total days' supply one authorization may cover, and how many open prescriptions of one medication and strength a patient may hold.

**1. Definitions.**
1.1 *Largest days' supply per fill* — the most days one fill may dispense (whole days).
1.2 *Refills per authorization* — the refills one new prescription or renewal authorizes in addition to the first fill (a count).
1.3 *Validity period* — the calendar days after which the prescription expires, counted from the prescribing or renewal date with that date itself as day one; the expiration date is the last day of that count.
1.4 *Total days' supply per authorization* — the largest total days' supply one prescription or renewal may authorize across all of its fills (whole days).
1.5 *Open prescriptions of the same medication* — the most open prescriptions of the same medication and strength one patient may hold.

**2. Schedule by class.**

| Class | Largest days' supply per fill | Refills per authorization | Validity period (calendar days) | Total days' supply per authorization | Open prescriptions of one medication and strength |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acute Short-Course Prescription | 14 | 0 | 30 | 14 | 1 |
| Standard Maintenance Prescription | 90 | 3 | 365 | 360 | 1 |
| Monitored Maintenance Prescription | 90 | 3 | 365 | 360 | 1 |
| Schedule III-V Controlled Prescription | 30 | 5 | 180 | 180 | 1 |
| Schedule II Controlled Prescription | 30 | 0 | 90 | 90 | 1 |
| Specialty Medication Prescription | 30 | 11 | 365 | 360 | 1 |

**3. Notes on the schedule.**
3.1 A class with 0 refills per authorization (the Acute Short-Course Prescription and the Schedule II Controlled Prescription) authorizes the first fill only.
3.2 The two maintenance classes have identical limits in this schedule; they differ in other schedules of the line.

**4. Worked illustration (hypothetical dates).** A Schedule II Controlled Prescription signed on a hypothetical 1 March has a validity period of 90 calendar days with 1 March as day one: March supplies days 1 to 31, April days 32 to 61, and 29 May is day 90, so its expiration date is 29 May. A Standard Maintenance Prescription renewed on a hypothetical 10 January of a non-leap year counts 365 days with 10 January as day one and expires on 9 January of the following year.
